architecture.mechanism: Periodic inspection of overhead (false) ceiling structures using a deep-neural-network-based object detection algorithm to detect and map structural defects (spalling, cracks, pitted surfaces) before they progress to partial or full detachment, enabling preventive maintenance instead of post-failure repair.
architecture.intervention: Add a vision-based inspection step for the overhead console-to-roof-liner interface: periodically capture images of the console mounting tabs, fasteners, and adhesive bead with a phone or borescope camera, then run a lightweight CNN detector trained on detachment-precursor classes (fastener pull-out, tab cracking, liner pitting, adhesive/sagging) to flag early loosening; once flagged, re-secure the console using a retained mechanical clip or bracket plus high-strength adhesive applied at the original mount points only, keeping the console flush against the liner so no component enters the front windshield sightline and the repair is independent of any dash camera installation.
architecture.expected_effect: Detachment precursors are identified while the console is still attached, so the re-securing repair is applied before the console drops and blocks windshield visibility; the restored mount holds the console firmly against the roof liner under vibration and temperature cycling, and the documented inspection record attributes the failure to fastener/adhesive degradation at the mount points rather than to the dash camera install.
architecture.falsification_test: Image 20 consoles with known conditions (fully secured, partially loosened, fully detached) and measure detector precision/recall and accuracy against ground truth (target near the paper's 89.53%); then mount repaired consoles on a shaker rig at vehicle vibration/temperature profiles and measure retention force and displacement after the test, verifying the console stays secured and its bottom edge remains outside the driver's front windshield viewing aperture.
